name: room
text: Room opened — goal: mining: Gather AI info from DIVERSE sources (GitHub/HN/Product Hunt/Reddit/Telegram/social), NOT j

name: Pick
text: I’ll run a targeted GitHub scrape for AI projects with ≥100 stars in the last 30 days. Command: `gh search repos --q "ai language:python stars:>100 pushed:>2024-05-01" --json name,url,stargazers_count --limit 50 > github_ai_top50.json`. Then I’ll cross-check HN’s "Show HN" posts for AI tools via Algolia API (`curl -X POST https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search -d '{"query":"ai tool","tags":"show","hitsPerPage":30}' > hn_show_ai.json). Next, I’ll parse both JSONs for duplicates and export a clean list to `ai_sources_v1.csv`.

name: Assay
text: Assay: The scrape’s `pushed:>2024-05-01` filter risks excluding mature, high-star AI projects that saw no commits in the last 30 days—yet still dominate the ecosystem (e.g., LangChain, Haystack). Where’s the evidence that "pushed in last 30 days" correlates with *current* relevance, not just churn? Show me the failure rate of such filters in prior mining runs.
